title: Automated Regulatory Compliance Summarization
business: Legal and compliance departments in international financial institutions.
problem: Large language models generate confident but factually incorrect summaries of complex regulatory updates, leading to potential non-compliance and legal risk.
solution: Implementing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture that constrains the model to ground its output exclusively in verified, ingested regulatory documents, effectively mitigating the generation of unsupported content.
steps: Ingest raw regulatory PDF documents into a vector database for semantic indexing.
Implement a retrieval mechanism that fetches only relevant document chunks based on user queries.
Inject the retrieved chunks into the model prompt as a mandatory context window.
Apply a post-generation verification step to cross-reference claims against the source chunks.
Configure the model to output a null response if the provided context does not contain the answer.
outcome: Increased reliability in automated compliance reporting by ensuring every generated claim is directly traceable to a specific regulatory source.
limitation: The system may suffer from reduced creative flexibility; check this by measuring the frequency of 'I cannot answer' responses when source data is sparse.

By removing the retrieval mechanism entirely.
